note: Length and body form from Engelman 2023/2024 (fineness 2.7-3.2); lunate fin and pelagic cruising from Ferron et al. 2017. Speeds are our lamnid-analogue allometry (mako 0.45 BL/s at 2 m, scaled L^0.6; burst 0.9x4sqrt(L)).

mode: subcarangiform slow cruiser, ram suspension feeder
note: Suspension feeding per Coatham et al. 2020; basking-shark analogue (filter cruise ~0.85 m/s, breach 5 m/s vertical, Johnston 2018). Repo baseline 5 m; Engelman 2023 ~4 m; 7 m is the older reconstruction.
Ferron et al. 2017 treat it as a bottom-ambush arthrodire; 29.6-39.4 cm (Miles & Westoll 1968). Cruise 0.9 L^0.6 with armour discount; burst 0.75x4sqrt(L).

mode: benthic; rigid box, slender heterocercal tail, pectoral props
note: Bechard et al. 2014: no head-thorax joint, constrained pectoral articulation; B. rex reaches 1.7 m (Downs 2016). Armoured-benthic cruise k=0.35; burst 0.6x4sqrt(L). Jointed pectorals allow a slow push-back.
Ray-like disc with upward mouth, ambush from the bottom; skate/ray analogues cruise ~1 disc-length/s, pivot on the spot and can reverse the fin wave. 30-100 cm range.

mode: rigid delta-wing shield + hypocercal tail, near-bottom
note: Ferron et al. 2024 CFD: ground-effect lift on a 15 cm shield, benthic boundary-layer swimmer. No paired fins, so no sculling and no backing. Burst 0.85x4sqrt(L).

mode: carangiform/thunniform-ish, tall lunate tail, pelagic pursuit
note: Near-symmetrical lunate tail, prey swallowed head-first (Frey 2023; Cleveland Shale material). Mako analogue measured: 2 m, cruise 0.9 m/s, burst 5.0 m/s (Nosal 2024). Shark cruise k=0.6; burst 4sqrt(L). Sharks do not back up.
Spine-brush adds drag and fins are small: probably a slow-moving shark. Cruise k~0.5; burst 0.65x4sqrt(L). Max 3 m is S. productus; asset is a 0.7 m Stethacanthus sp. (CMNH 8988).
Fusiform early actinopterygian with a large gape; teleost-like rules k=0.9 and 4sqrt(L). 30-55 cm (Pearson & Westoll 1979 via Wikipedia; Giles 2015).

Gogo dipnoans are 30-60 cm; R. kimberleyensis concretion ~12.5 cm of skull and girdle (Clement 2012). Modern lungfish cruise well under 1 BL/s and back up with pectoral fins; flexible body turns tightly.
O. jandemarrai known from 47 cm (head 10 cm) with larger material to ~2 m (Andrews 2006); O. sigmoides ~3-4 m. Grouper-like ambush: low cruise, strong lunge (0.9x4sqrt(L)).

mode: subcarangiform in shallows, bottom-propped on pectoral fins
note: 1.25-2.75 m (Daeschler 2006); enlarged pelvis for shallow-water body support (Shubin 2014). Crocodile-like: slow, with a short lunge. Pectoral fins push it back slowly.
60 cm, deep finned tail, paddle limbs; all known specimens juvenile (Sanchez 2016). Salamander analogue: flexible body, tight turns, slow limb-paddled reverse.

Phacopid queue models give 0.5-2 cm/s walking (Song 2021; Trenchard 2017); 1-10 cm typical, ~13 cm largest. Legged: pivots in place, steps backward slowly. Burst is our estimate; enrolment is the real defence.
4-10 cm including a trident about as long as the body; same gait as Eldredgeops with extra drag and a long lever ahead of the pivot.

mode: drag-based paddle rowing with lift; bottom walking
note: 2.5 m from a 46 cm claw (Braddy 2008); Plotnick 1985 paddle-tip ceiling ~1 m/s for a much smaller eurypterid; in-phase backstroke rowing (Vrazo 2018). Paddles can row asymmetrically or in reverse. Speeds are our estimate under that ceiling.

Nebalia-model phyllocarid (Bergstrom 1987): natatory pleopods, flexible abdomen, furcal rami. 'jet' here means the crustacean tail-flip: the fast direction is backward (~1 m/s for shrimp of this size). 12-15 cm.

mode: podial walking (tube feet), no arm rowing
note: Clark 2020: lacks the arm joints needed for rowing, so slower than Ophiocoma's measured 2 cm/s (Astley 2012). Length is arm-tip span. Any arm can lead, so turning and reversing are free but slow.
Body >=12.5 cm, leg span ~32 cm, flattened paddle legs of alternating size (Bergstrom 1980); living pycnogonids swim by slow leg beats or sink with legs tucked.

Nautilus analogue measured: 0.35-1.6 BL/s, ~0.08 m/s (Neil & Askew 2018); compressed narrow-ventered conch is low-drag in Westermann morphospace. Funnel swivels so it turns in place, slowly; backward is the fast direction. Shell diameters 7-17 cm.

mode: jet, vertically stable orthocone; upward dodge escape
note: Peterman & Ritterbush 2021 57 cm model: 0.88 BL/s vertical with cruising thrust, 2.85 BL/s with peak thrust; horizontal reorientation wastes thrust to rocking. Devonian Michelinoceras material is fragmentary; 0.5 m is a working value, 1 m a large orthocerid.
